  4. I had a fatty boss who always tried to offer food. Now, in my mind, "No." or "No thanks." are impolite for me to say, and I feel obligated to give a reason. For example, if my boss says "hey can you come in on Thursday" I won't say "Sorry, no." or "Sorry, I can't." Instead, I always explain myself. I know about 30 or so years ago, one of the scientific beliefs for parents were "If you have a single child with Autism, you have a good chance of having multiple children with Autism". I have 5 siblings, 4 of us (Myself included) are all autistic, so I can see some validity with it being a genetic thing in some capacity.

Does a fat / obese pregnancy cause Autism? Couldn't say, but I don't think it was the main thing causing it before.

On another note, I find that this generation as a whole has been developing in a bad and less social way, (IE Gamers, Keyboard warriors etc) and it can be quite hard for people to tell the difference between someone with Autism and any of the aforementioned, which can lead to people being unable to tell them apart from one another (This generally includes fats tbh).

Oh there's no one answer to Autism and other neurological disorders, but there are certain things that can increase the risk and obesity is one of them. Doesn't mean you'd have to be obese to have an autistic child, but it does mean if a woman was obese during pregnancy than her child is very likely to develop autism whereas normal weight women have a lower risk.

Personally, I would need decades more research to definitively say one way or the other, but we can't ignore the data we have already. It is a fact, obese mothers are far more likely to cause their unborn baby to have neurological disorders then normal weight people.

As for "more autism" I think it is a combination of things. The obesity thing is one. The "now we know how to diagnose the previously undiagnosed" is another. Genetic makeup will always be a factor. We know vaccinations are NOT a cause, but there are likely still many factor out there to be taken into account. In many cases if a child is autistic that's just how they were always going to be, and that is okay. But I know one thing for sure; if I became obese then had an autistic child, I'd always wonder if my bad habits were to blame. We love our children no matter who or what they are, but we should do everything in our power to protect and nurture them.

Not drinking during pregnancy, not being obese during pregnancy, eating healthy while pregnant, not smoking, not working in the pits of a coal mine.... there is a lot we are told we can do to increase our child's chance of a good life. We can't do everything of course, your family having autism if your mother wasn't ever obese is one of those cases. Just like how my mother had nothing to do with my heart condition. Sometimes it just happens.

But most people agree life would be a little easier on our kids if we can manage to avoid these things, so any steps a woman can take to ensure her children are as healthy as possible shouldn't even be a question in her mind.
